question.problem:
Consider the function $f(x,y)=\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡(x-y)}{{e}^{x+y}}.$ The partial derivative of $f$ with respect to $x$ is given by

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=\frac{h(x,y)}{{e}^{x+y}}.
$$

Find the function $h(x,y).$
question.worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $x,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

Using the quotient and chain rules, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡(x-y)}{{e}^{x+y}}) \\  & =\frac{\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{tan}⁡(x-y))\cdot {e}^{x+y}-\operatorname{tan}⁡(x-y)\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{x+y})}{{({e}^{x+y})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡(x-y)\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(x-y)\cdot {e}^{x+y}-\operatorname{tan}⁡(x-y)\cdot {e}^{x+y}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(x+y)}{{({e}^{x+y})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡(x-y)\cdot 1\cdot {e}^{x+y}-\operatorname{tan}⁡(x-y)\cdot {e}^{x+y}\cdot 1}{{({e}^{x+y})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{({sec}^{2}⁡(x-y)-\operatorname{tan}⁡(x-y)){e}^{x+y}}{{({e}^{x+y})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡(x-y)-\operatorname{tan}⁡(x-y)}{{e}^{x+y}}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
h(x,y)={sec}^{2}⁡(x-y)-\operatorname{tan}⁡(x-y).
$$
